Erdheim-Chester disease: Laboratory studies: White-cell count and differential: normal
Laboratory studies: Hemoglobin: normal
Laboratory studies: Renal and liver function tests: normal
Laboratory studies: Tumor markers and autoimmune serologies: negative
No granulomas or malignant cells were identified
Demographics: 36-year-old man
Chief complaint: 4-year history of diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows and intermittent generalized pruritus
Symptom progression: bone pain worsened and developed blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking over the past 2 months
Laboratory studies: Platelet count: mild thrombocytosis (120 × 10^9/L)
Laboratory studies: C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: mildly elevated
Radiographic studies: Knee radiographs: bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes of the distal femora and proximal tibiae
Radiographic studies: Humeral radiographs: intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri
Radiographic studies: Forearm radiographs (lateral view): sclerosis of the proximal ulnae and radii without fracture

Nuclear and cross-sectional imaging: 99mTc bone scintigraphy and FDG-PET: bilateral symmetric uptake in long bones, right clavicle, and mandible, with uptake in subcutaneous and muscle tissues of the lower limbs
Nuclear and cross-sectional imaging: CT and MRI of the lower limbs: multifocal intramedullary sclerosis of the femora and tibiae
Nuclear and cross-sectional imaging: MRI of the brain: enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues
Nuclear and cross-sectional imaging: PET/CT of the brain: corresponding FDG-avid lesions
Nuclear and cross-sectional imaging: CT and PET/CT of the abdomen: bilateral perinephric soft-tissue thickening with FDG uptake
Biopsy results: diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells
Immunohistochemical staining: positive for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa, and negative for CD1a, S100, and langerin
